title: Cap. III Sol. Rat. 9 close: can destine glory depending on others' sins without prior foresight to confer
pass_a_gloss: False therefore was what had been assumed in the argument, namely, that that glory which somehow depends on the sins of others cannot be decreed except from such foresight. For it can be decreed or destined, although it cannot be conferred, except with foresight of this sort going before.
pass_b_english: So the argument's assumption was false — that glory which somehow depends on others' sins cannot be decreed except from such foresight. It can be decreed or destined without that; it is only the conferring that cannot happen unless foresight of that sort goes first.
source_text: Falsum ergo fuit quod in argumento assumptum erat, nempe, non posse eam gloriam, quae aliquo modo dependet ex peccatis aliorum, decerni nisi ex tali praescientia. Decerni enim vel destinari potest, quamvis non conferri, nisi hujusmodi praescientia praeeunte.
notes: Densify De praedestinatione Cap. III Rat. 9 section 316. Pass A!=B. Packet praedestinatione_cap3_rat9_densify. Honest partial.
